claimMap.claim: Four named subscribers filed a September 18 complaint against four named companies.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Four paying AI subscribers filed a proposed class-action complaint on September 18 against Anthropic, OpenAI OpCo, SpaceXAI and Google.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: CHARLES BUIST, CHEYENNE HUNT, CHRISTINE BULLOCK, and NICK SPETSAS ... v. ANTHROPIC, PBC; OPENAI OPCO, LLC; SPACEXAI LLC; AND GOOGLE LLC.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Caption and filing stamp identify the named parties and September 18 filing; this is a filing fact only.

claimMap.claim: Plaintiffs allege coordination slowed competing AI product improvement and reduced prior subscription value; the filing does not resolve that claim.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The plaintiffs allege the companies agreed to slow improvements to competing AI products, reducing the value of subscriptions people had already bought. A filing records that allegation; it does not decide whether an agreement happened, whether it was unlawful, or what remedy would follow.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: This action challenges an agreement among the four companies at the frontier of artificial intelligence—Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google—to slow the pace at which each company improves the competing products it sells to consumers.

The value of those subscriptions consists of access to Defendants’ most capable models and to the improvements Defendants continually release. Defendants market and price those subscriptions on exactly that basis. An agreement that slows improvement lowers the quality of what subscribers receive for the price they pay.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Paragraphs 1 and 14 supply plaintiffs’ allegation; the story explicitly withholds a finding of agreement, legality, or remedy.

claimMap.claim: The complaint identifies an Amodei September 12 call as part of plaintiffs’ pleaded sequence.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The complaint points to a September 12 public call by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to slow AI capability improvements. That is the plaintiffs’ account of the sequence, not proof of a cross-company agreement.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: On the morning of September 12, 2026, Anthropic’s Chief Executive Officer, Dario Amodei, published an essay titled We Must Pace the Frontier. It declared: “We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models.” It called for “industry-wide coordination” among frontier laboratories.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: This is the complaint’s pleaded account of the sequence, not independent proof of a cross-company agreement.

claimMap.claim: The complaint says it does not seek to stop companies from independently taking safety measures or slowing their own work.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Their complaint draws a narrow line: it says it does not seek to stop a company from taking its own safety measures or slowing its own development.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Plaintiffs do not seek to prohibit any Defendant from independently adopting safety measures or product guardrails, independently slowing or suspending its own development.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Paragraph 151 states the pleaded limit; it is not a ruling about any company’s conduct.

claimMap.claim: Plaintiffs request class certification, damages and injunctive relief, none of which filing grants.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The plaintiffs ask for class certification, damages and an order stopping the alleged agreement; filing the request does not approve or grant any of them.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The Class consists of all persons in the United States who ... purchased an individual subscription ... Plaintiffs request certification, damages and injunctive relief.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: The complaint requests these remedies; the story does not report certification or awarded relief.

claimMap.claim: The complaint pleads a Sherman Act claim against all defendants.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Antitrust is the area of law the plaintiffs invoke in arguing that the alleged agreement restrained competition.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1 (Against All Defendants).

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: The filing identifies its legal theory; the story offers no legal advice or court conclusion.
